explanation.title: Spanish Non-Finite Verb Forms: Infinitive, Gerund & Participle

sections.subtitle: Infinitive Usage
sections.content:
📋 The Infinitive (-ar, -er, -ir)

🎯 Five Main Uses:

1️⃣ Subject of sentence:
→ Nadar es divertido (Swimming is fun)

2️⃣ After conjugated verbs:
→ Quiero comer (I want to eat)
→ Puedo hablar (I can speak)

3️⃣ After 'al' (upon/when):
→ Al llegar, vi a Juan (Upon arriving, I saw Juan)

4️⃣ As noun (NOT gerund like English):
→ Me gusta bailar (I like dancing/to dance)

5️⃣ In impersonal expressions:
→ Es importante estudiar (It's important to study)

⚡ Critical Difference from English:
Spanish uses infinitive (not gerund) as noun

sections.subtitle: Infinitive After Prepositions
sections.content:
📋 Major Difference from English!

✅ The Rule:
• After prepositions → use INFINITIVE (not gerund)

💡 Common Patterns:
• antes de + inf (before doing)
• después de + inf (after doing)
• para + inf (in order to)
• sin + inf (without doing)
• al + inf (upon doing)

💡 Examples:
→ Antes de comer (Before eating)
→ Para estudiar (In order to study)
→ Sin hablar (Without speaking)
→ Después de llegar (After arriving)

⚠️ Exception:
Only 'en' can be followed by gerund
→ Insistir en hacer (insist on doing)

🎯 Remember:
Preposition + INFINITIVE (not -ing!)
Unlike English!

sections.subtitle: Gerund Formation & Usage
sections.content:
📋 Gerund Formation

✅ Regular Formation:
• -AR verbs → -ando
→ hablar → hablando

• -ER/-IR verbs → -iendo
→ comer → comiendo
→ vivir → viviendo

⚠️ Irregular Gerunds:

-IR stem-changers:
• e → i: pedir → pidiendo
• o → u: dormir → durmiendo

Vowel stems (add 'y'):
• leer → leyendo
• caer → cayendo
• ir → yendo

🎯 Three Main Uses:

1️⃣ Progressive tenses with estar:
→ Estoy comiendo (I am eating)

2️⃣ After seguir/continuar:
→ Sigue estudiando (He keeps studying)

3️⃣ Show manner/how:
→ Salió corriendo (He left running)

⚡ NOT used as noun (use infinitive instead)!

sections.subtitle: Past Participle Formation
sections.content:
📋 Past Participle Formation

✅ Regular Formation:
• -AR → -ado
→ hablar → hablado

• -ER/-IR → -ido
→ comer → comido
→ vivir → vivido

⚠️ Accent if stem ends in vowel:
→ leer → leído
→ traer → traído
→ oír → oído
→ caer → caído

⚠️ Common Irregulars:
• abrir → abierto
• cubrir → cubierto
• decir → dicho
• escribir → escrito
• hacer → hecho
• morir → muerto
• poner → puesto
• romper → roto
• ver → visto
• volver → vuelto

💡 Compounds Follow Base:
→ describir → descrito
→ devolver → devuelto
→ descubrir → descubierto

sections.subtitle: Participles as Adjectives
sections.content:
📋 Past Participles as Adjectives

✅ Agreement Rule:
• Agree in gender/number with nouns

💡 Examples:
→ puerta cerrada (closed door)
→ libros escritos (written books)
→ ventanas abiertas (open windows)
→ problemas resueltos (solved problems)

🎯 Two Main Constructions:

1️⃣ With ESTAR (resultant state):
→ La puerta está cerrada
  (The door is closed - result)

2️⃣ With SER (passive voice):
→ La casa fue construida
  (The house was built - action)

💡 Common Adjective Participles:
• cansado (tired)
• aburrido (bored)
• emocionado (excited)
• perdido (lost)
• roto (broken)
• preocupado (worried)

sections.subtitle: Perfect Constructions with Haber
sections.content:
📋 Haber + Past Participle = Perfect Tenses

⚡ Critical Rule:
Participle is INVARIABLE (doesn't agree)

✅ Perfect Tense Forms:

• Present perfect:
→ he comido (I have eaten)
→ has visto (you have seen)

• Past perfect:
→ había comido (I had eaten)

• Future perfect:
→ habré comido (I will have eaten)

• Conditional perfect:
→ habría comido (I would have eaten)

• Present perfect subjunctive:
→ haya comido (that I have eaten)

• Pluperfect subjunctive:
→ hubiera comido (that I had eaten)

⚠️ Word Order Rule:
NEVER place anything between haber and participle

✅ Correct:
→ He comido ya (I have already eaten)

❌ Wrong:
→ He ya comido

questions.question: What are the three infinitive endings in Spanish?
questions.hint: The three verb groups: hablar, comer, vivir.

questions.question: 'Nadar es divertido' - Why use infinitive?

answers.text: Infinitive used as subject of sentence

questions.hint: Swimming (nadar) is the subject. Spanish uses infinitive, not gerund.

questions.question: 'Me gusta bailar' means 'I like dancing/to dance' - Why infinitive not gerund?

answers.text: Spanish uses infinitive as noun, not gerund

questions.hint: Major difference from English: Spanish uses infinitive where English uses gerund (-ing).

questions.question: What form follows prepositions in Spanish?
questions.hint: Unlike English: Spanish uses infinitive after prepositions (antes de comer).

questions.question: 'Antes de comer' means...
questions.hint: Antes de + infinitive. Prepositions take infinitive in Spanish.

questions.question: 'Sin hablar' means...
questions.hint: Sin + infinitive = without doing something.

questions.question: How do you form the gerund for -AR verbs?
questions.hint: hablar → hablando. Use -ando ending for -AR verbs.

questions.question: How do you form the gerund for -ER/-IR verbs?
questions.hint: comer → comiendo, vivir → viviendo. Use -iendo for -ER/-IR.

questions.question: What is the gerund of 'hablar'?
questions.hint: Remove -ar, add -ando: hablar → hablando.

questions.question: What is the irregular gerund of 'pedir' (e→i stem change)?
questions.hint: -IR stem-changers: e→i in gerund. Pedir → pidiendo.

questions.question: What is the irregular gerund of 'dormir' (o→u stem change)?
questions.hint: -IR stem-changers: o→u in gerund. Dormir → durmiendo.

questions.question: 'Estoy comiendo' uses gerund for...
questions.hint: Estar + gerund = progressive 'I am eating'.

questions.question: How do you form the past participle for -AR verbs?
questions.hint: hablar → hablado. Use -ado for -AR verbs.

questions.question: How do you form the past participle for -ER/-IR verbs?
questions.hint: comer → comido, vivir → vivido. Use -ido for -ER/-IR.

questions.question: What is the irregular past participle of 'hacer'?
questions.hint: Very common irregular: hacer → hecho (done/made).

questions.question: What is the irregular past participle of 'abrir'?
questions.hint: Irregular: abrir → abierto (opened).

questions.question: 'La puerta cerrada' - Why does 'cerrada' have -a ending?

answers.text: Past participle as adjective agrees with noun (feminine)

questions.hint: Participles as adjectives agree in gender/number: puerta (fem) → cerrada.

questions.question: 'Libros escritos' - Why does 'escritos' have -os ending?

answers.text: Participle as adjective agrees with plural masculine noun

questions.hint: Participles agree: libros (masc plural) → escritos (-os ending).

questions.question: 'La puerta está cerrada' vs 'La puerta es cerrada' - What's the difference?

answers.text: Estar = resultant state; Ser = passive action
Estar is wrong, only use ser
Estar is temporary, ser is permanent

questions.hint: Estar + participle = result/state. Ser + participle = passive voice/action.

questions.question: What is the structure of perfect tenses in Spanish?
questions.hint: Use auxiliary haber + past participle. Participle never changes.

questions.question: 'He comido' - Does 'comido' agree with subject gender/number?

answers.text: No, participles with haber are invariable

questions.hint: With haber, participle NEVER changes: he/hemos/has comido (always same).

questions.question: 'He ya comido' or 'He comido ya' - which is correct?

answers.text: He comido ya (nothing between haber and participle)
He ya comido (adverb between is fine)

questions.hint: Never separate haber and participle. Adverbs go after: He comido ya.

questions.question: What is the past participle of 'leer' (watch for accent!)?
questions.hint: Stem ends in vowel, so add accent: leer → leído (le-í-do).
